card: Executes a scripted-diff to strip trailing newline characters from one-line logging macros across 72 files and moves a logging test into the dedicated logging test suite. The author describes this as a longstanding low-priority style cleanup intended to eliminate manual reformatting and assist with log injection cleanup. No dependencies are noted.
evidence: Author notes: "This is a low-prio style cleanup for years, but: It is tedious and possibly distracting to do it manually when touching the line for other reasons" and cites related discussions on log injection in PR #35833 (PR description)
problem: Logging calls frequently contain unnecessary trailing newlines, causing style inconsistencies, clutter in unrelated PRs when modified manually, and complications in discussions around log escaping and injection.

risk.why: Only modifies logging format strings via automated regex and moves a test file, carrying minimal operational risk.

scope_notes: Contains a large mechanical scripted-diff modifying single-line log strings across 72 files, verifiable using the sed script in the commit message.
summary: Removes trailing newline escape sequences from one-line logging invocations across the codebase via a scripted-diff. Also moves the LogEscapeMessage unit test from util tests into logging tests.
